newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Canal revenues rise despite less traffic.
newsitem.headline: Panama Canal revenues rise despite less traffic.

text.p: Panama Canal toll revenues edged up 1.5 percent to $374.3 million in the nine months to June 30 despite a drop in traffic, authorities said Wednesday.

The Panama Canal Commission (PCC) said in a statement that traffic from October 1996 to June 1997 fell 4.5 percent to 10,017 oceangoing transits, or an average 36.7 daily transits, compared with the corresponding period the previous year.

"International trade and the international economy are cyclical, and so is traffic through the Panama Canal. This has affected canal transits," the commission's associate director, Franklin Castrellon, told Reuters.
He said the canal remained highly competitive in terms of value for money and efficiency.
Toll revenues for June fell 3.8 percent to $38 million from $39.5 million the same month last year. Tolls were increased 8.2 percent on January 1.
Traffic in June 1997 fell 8.3 percent to 1,024 transits, or an average 34.1 daily transits.

The Panama Canal Commission is a U.S. government agency which runs the waterway connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. The United States is obliged by treaty to hand over the canal to Panama on December 31, 1999.
(( -- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507 223 7739))
